_readme: Animation clips and directions. A 'generated' clip asks Mage-Flow-Edit for each frame separately, using the character's sprite (and a canonical view of the direction) as references. A clip with a 'guide' (the walk) first draws a puppet of each pose (npcgen/pose.py) and has the model repaint it as the character, except in styles with 'guided_walk': false, which use its 'poses' like any other clip. 'poses' maps a direction group (side = left/right, front = down/up) to a frame count and one pose phrase per frame. A 'procedural' clip is derived from the canonical view without generating anything. 'cycle' is how long one loop takes in seconds, so the frame rate follows the frame count. Experimental clips have one reviewed draft GPU sample and remain unvalidated across characters and styles; quality_note describes that sample's issues.

canonical_prompts.right: Show the same character in a side view facing right, standing still in a neutral relaxed pose with arms at the sides, full body head to toe
canonical_prompts.left: Show the same character in a side view facing left, standing still in a neutral relaxed pose with arms at the sides, full body head to toe
canonical_prompts.up: Show the same character from directly behind, back view facing away from the camera, standing still in a neutral relaxed pose with arms at the sides, full body head to toe

reference_strategy._note: Which images to pass as references for the frames of each direction, in order. 'front' is the character's sprite, 'canonical' the generated view for that direction. Measured on a pixel-art test character (leg variation: 0 = static, ~0.3 = a real walk): for side views front-only drifted (the hair changed between frames) and canonical-only barely moved (0.06), but both together gave real movement (0.33) with a stable head. For the back view the canonical view made the legs static (0.07-0.09) and front-only walked (0.23), so it uses the sprite alone. Re-test if you change the style or the model.

guided_strategy._note: References for the frames of a guided clip, after the drawn pose (which is always the FIRST image). Measured on a photoreal test character: the sprite alone kept the character the same across a cycle; a canonical side view as a third image made the model copy the puppet instead.

guided_prompt: Repaint the rough figure in the first image as a finished painting of the {who} in the second image, {verb} {view}, {caught}full body head to toe, on {backdrop} with no floor and no shadow. Keep the exact pose of the rough figure: the same leg, knee, foot and arm positions.{note} The whole figure, from the top of the head to both shoes, fits inside the picture with space around it. {keep}, as in the second image.

guided_notes._note: Extra wording per direction, for every frame ('caught', 'note') or for one kind of pose ('by_pose'). A front pose barely differs from the standing sprite, which is the second image, so without the front wording the model drew the standing sprite four times (measured: the legs differed from it by 0.02-0.05; with it 0.27-0.40). The passing step is often drawn as a small stride; with the sentence the feet came out 0.12-0.28 of the height apart at four seeds, without it 0.24-0.38.

down.note: The pose changes from the standing picture: copy the rough figure's legs and arms exactly, including the raised knee and the foot lifted off the ground.

by_pose.passing: The legs pass each other: one leg is straight and carries the weight, the other knee is bent and that foot is lifted off the ground right beside the standing leg, so the feet are close together.
The legs pass each other: one leg is straight and carries the weight, the other knee is bent and that foot is lifted off the ground right beside the standing leg, so the feet are close together.
